feasibility: Can eligible opaque tasks be supplied and executed with complete acceptance, failure, isolation, and usage records?
Can deterministic quality gates and the corrective protocol run reproducibly within the fixed timeout?
variance_and_measurement: What between-task and within-task variation, arm discordance, timeout frequency, and missingness would a later confirmatory design need to accommodate?
Are task-level cost and token distributions measurable without conflating provider cache pricing with agent work?
exploratory_policy_effect: What is the task-level distribution of exploratory differences between default Codex and C-short v0.1 under identical subject configuration?

excluded_arms.reason: negative development variant with no acceptance advantage over C-short v0.1 and no evidence-based Pilot question

task_supply.partition_rule: Within each frozen stratum, rank opaque IDs by SHA-256 of partition_seed, a NUL byte, and task ID; allocate the first three to Pilot and retain at least the next three unseen for confirmatory planning.
task_supply.run_order_rule: Rank task-and-repetition blocks by SHA-256 of partition_seed, a NUL byte, task ID, a NUL byte, and repetition ID; run both arms adjacently within each block and alternate baseline-first/short-first, with the starting arm selected by the low bit of SHA-256(partition_seed plus a NUL byte plus arm-order).

subject_configuration.permissions: automatic approval review with workspace-write sandbox
subject_configuration.session_persistence: fresh per cell; retained only if required for the single corrective round
subject_configuration.corrective_feedback: On initial hidden-check failure, return only predeclared failing check names once, identically across arms; retain the initial failure and stop after the second evaluation.

reviewers.permitted_quality_evidence: exact hidden checks, repository regression tests, existing lint/type/build checks, evaluator/config protection, seeded guard retention, and seeded shared-root-cause checks

variance: task-level cost and token distribution where available

version_and_retention.policy_change_after_pilot_outcomes: Creates a new exploratory policy version; retain old runs and never combine effect estimates across incompatible versions.
